evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/ai/ocr.rs:261-312 — submit_correction (POST /api/v1/ai/ocr/correction) authorizes only by checking the caller is_member of the CLIENT-SUPPLIED body.organization_id (OcrCorrectionRequest.organization_id: Uuid, line 52), then persists a correction whose body.meter_reading_id (Option<Uuid>, line 58) is NEVER validated to belong to that org. The referenced reading's tenant is never checked.

backend/crates/db/src/repositories/meter.rs:1140-1157 — create_ocr_correction does a bare INSERT INTO ocr_meter_corrections binding organization_id and meter_reading_id straight from the request with no WHERE/EXISTS ownership guard, so nothing downstream closes the gap. A member of org A can attach a correction to another tenant's meter_reading_id (poisoning cross-tenant correction/training data and creating cross-tenant referential links).

Contrast with the sibling handler process_meter_reading (ocr.rs:177-195) which DOES verify meter.organization_id membership before writing — submit_correction omits the equivalent meter_reading->org check, making the gap an in-file inconsistency, not an intentional design.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/ai/ocr.rs:125-312 — both ai/ocr handlers use the AuthUser extractor plus client-supplied body.organization_id and manual org_member_repo.is_member() checks, opting OUT of the RLS WITH CHECK boundary that every other ai/ handler relies on: equipment.rs (org = rls.tenant_id(), lines 62/86/110/139/167), workflows.rs:434, sessions.rs, voice.rs:65 all derive the authoritative org from the token via RlsConnection. ocr.rs is the lone segment outlier.

This per-handler opt-out is the root cause enabling code-review-ai-ocr-correction-idor: because the org is taken from the request body rather than rls.tenant_id() and RLS is not in the write path, the ownership invariant must be re-implemented by hand — and one branch (submit_correction) forgot. Recommend migrating both ocr handlers to RlsConnection/rls.tenant_id() so the DB policy enforces tenant scoping uniformly.
